topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Audit logs, log retention and redaction
summary: Initial discovery focused on whether Hawthorn should use Redwood Hosted, Dedicated or Private for an upcoming lending assistant product. Main concerns: PII handling, log retention and redaction, KMS key residency, and compliance evidence for auditors. Agreed to share compliance artifacts and scope a pilot to validate performance and residency controls.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Hawthorn HoP), Tom Erickson (Sec Arch), Priya Singh (PM), Sam Ortiz (DevOps)

Summary: quick intake to map security constraints and fit for hosted/dedicated/private. Customer strongly regulated, mix of EU/US customers, HIPAA for a vertical pipeline in beta.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, then Luca and I will surface the options and we want to understand your constraints and timeline.
[00:12] Aisha Rahman: Hi hi, Aisha here. we run lending and underwriting flows, lots of customer PII and sometimes health-related docs for specific partners so HIPAA matters for those pockets. we're evaluating hosting options for inference and want to map compliance scope.
[00:26] Tom Erickson: Tom, security. key question for us is where keys and logs live, and can we ensure that logs with PII never leave our control. also auditors will want chain of custody.
[00:39] Luca Patel: Great. high level: Redwood has Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity, isolated tenancy), and Private (VPC or on-prem control plane). there are tradeoffs: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value; Dedicated gives tenancy and SLA; Private gives you full control for keys and audit trails.
[00:58] Priya Singh: timeline-wise we aim to ship an internal pilot in Q4, but auditors kick off evidence collection in mid-October so this matters.
[01:10] Maya Chen: Noted. can you describe the flow where PII is seen? is it preprocessed before hitting the model, or do you expect raw documents to go into Redwood?
[01:22] Sam Ortiz: Currently raw ingestion pipeline, we scrub some fields but not completely; we'd like to ideally push redaction upstream but need options if something slips through.
[01:35] Tom Erickson: One core ask: we need to prevent persistent logs of raw PII in any third-party system. if logs are kept, they must be redacted and we need proof for auditors.
[01:48] Luca Patel: Understood. Hosted API by default stores request/response logs for a period for observability, but we have configurable retention and log redaction tooling and an option to disable persistent storage for certain tenants. Dedicated gives more control: logs can be routed to your s3 with server-side encryption, and Private gives you full control of the control plane and logs. note: there are subtle differences in telemetry traces vs platform audit logs.
[02:15] Aisha Rahman: can you elaborate on encryption keys? we need keys that never leave our region and ideally are customer-managed.
[02:27] Luca Patel: Yes, we support KMS integrations. Hosted supports customer-managed keys (CMKs) in supported cloud providers; keys can be configured per-account for encryption at rest. Dedicated can be tied to your own KMS with key policies that limit key usage to specific tenants. Private supports HSM/KMS on-prem or cloud-backed keys that never transit Redwood's managed control plane if you choose that architecture.
[02:53] Tom Erickson: And key residency? keys must be provisioned in EU for EU records. we can't have keys in US for EU data.
[03:02] Luca Patel: That's doable — region-locking of keys is part of our Private offering. for Hosted we have region-specific key residency for certain accounts, but it's more opinionated. we'll put the exact matrix in the SOC2/HIPAA pack.
[03:20] Priya Singh: auditors also ask for immutable audit trails — do you offer WORM style logs or append-only audit records?
[03:30] Luca Patel: We offer audit log shipping to customer-owned destinations (S3, GCS) where you can enable object lock / WORM. For Hosted, we can export and sign logs daily; Dedicated and Private give you direct control to enable object lock.
[03:46] Maya Chen: quick question on fallback behavior — if a region is out of capacity can requests fallback to another region temporarily? would that be a compliance issue?
[03:58] Sam Ortiz: That worries us. fallback across geographies would violate data residency.
[04:04] Luca Patel: We have routing policies per customer. by default we avoid cross-region fallback for datasets that are region-locked. auto-fallback is opt-in; we can disable cross-border fallbacks for your account.
[04:18] Tom Erickson: good. can you talk about caching/KV cache? tokens and KV caches might contain conversation context which can have PII. how is that handled?
[04:30] Luca Patel: Continuous KV cache is memory-resident on the serving node and not written to persistent logs by default. however for scaling we sometimes snapshot caches; for Dedicated/Private we can disable snapshots and keep everything ephemeral. for Hosted we offer prefixes caching with redaction and TTL. also we have a feature to hash or encrypt KV entries using customer keys before any optional snapshotting.
[05:00] Aisha Rahman: ok that's helpful. auditors will also want to see a data flow diagram and the points where PII can touch Redwood, including which microservices.
[05:10] Maya Chen: we'll share a DPIA-style diagram. Luca will add the service names and where audit logs are captured.
[05:18] Priya Singh: what about HIPAA de-identification? Our legal team says certain PHI elements must be purged within X days. can Redwood enforce time-based deletion?
[05:30] Luca Patel: Yes. we offer retention policies per-tenant. Hosted has configurable retention windows down to 0 days for certain log types but still needs a compliance review; Dedicated allows you to set retention and automatic purge pipelines; Private gives you full control. we can implement lifecycle rules that invoke secure delete and overwrite depending on storage backend.
[05:56] Tom Erickson: any certifications or attestations we can show auditors?
[06:03] Maya Chen: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II, and we can provide a HIPAA attestation and data processing addendum. we'll attach the compliance pack after the call.
[06:15] Aisha Rahman: are there any known limitations for models with sensitive content in hosted? e.g., moderation or PII leakage concerns?
[06:28] Luca Patel: The platform doesn't modify model weights; but we have prompt-layering and output filters. we can add post-processing redaction functions and an eval harness to test for PII leakage on your prompt sets.
[06:46] Priya Singh: that eval harness — can we run it on Dedicated? we want to see end-to-end.
[06:52] Luca Patel: absolutely. SE-led pilot can run on Dedicated or Private depending on how much control you need. usually we start with Dedicated to validate perf and isolation, then move to Private if you need full control over keys and control plane.
[07:06] Sam Ortiz: Perf: our peak inference patterns are short prompts but high qps, like 2k qps sustained bursts. what's the recommended capacity planning?
[07:18] Luca Patel: For 2k qps with short tokens, we typically recommend a dedicated GPU pool sized with continuous batching; we'll need your exact latency SLOs. we can provide initial capacity estimates after we see token mix and model choice.
[07:34] Tom Erickson: latency SLO — <100ms 95th for prediction. is that realistic across Dedicated?
[07:40] Luca Patel: It's achievable for short-context models on dedicated pools in the same region, assuming good batching configs. we'll run benchmarks to confirm.
[07:50] Aisha Rahman: let's surface legal concerns: we have subsidiaries in EU and the US. for EU customers we'd like data to never leave EU. can Redwood enforce tenant-level geographic blocks?
[08:02] Maya Chen: Yes — tenant-level geofence is supported. for Hosted we'll map accounts to a region, Dedicated you can reserve capacity in a given region, Private gives you full on-prem or VPC control.
[08:15] Priya Singh: Another auditor ask: proof of deletion. can you provide deletion certificates when data is purged?
[08:24] Luca Patel: We can emit deletion audit events with signatures and timestamps that can be exported to your log sink. for Private, you can also run a hash-based verification and we can include that in the report.
[08:37] Tom Erickson: OK. curious about network egress paths — do we have any third-party telemetry vendors that might receive meta?
[08:45] Luca Patel: No third-party telemetry by default. all telemetry stays within the Redwood control plane; for Hosted we have managed tracing but we can opt to route traces to your collector. Dedicated/Private make it easier to prevent third-party exposure.
[08:59] Aisha Rahman: what about the control plane understanding of payloads? does Redwood ever index request payloads for search or debugging?
[09:07] Luca Patel: No indexing of payloads for product analytics. we keep diagnostic metadata but not full request bodies unless you opt-in to enhanced debugging. and even then we have redaction rules.
[09:19] Priya Singh: If we move forward with a pilot, we'll need a contract addendum about log retention and key residency.
[09:26] Maya Chen: we can prepare a narrow MSA addendum covering retention, KMS, and region-locking.
[09:32] Tom Erickson: One edge case: legal hold. How do you support legal hold if we need to stop deletion for certain records?
[09:40] Luca Patel: We can suspend lifecycle deletes for specific records and mark them immutable in your exported audit store. for Hosted, this is possible via an override; for Dedicated/Private it's customer-managed.
[09:52] Aisha Rahman: any known migration friction from Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private? we may want to start hosted for speed then move.
[10:00] Luca Patel: We try to make migration seamless: model versioning and artifacts are portable. challenges are usually around KMS and network setup. if you plan to migrate, we recommend designing with tenancy and key separation from the start.
[10:15] Priya Singh: Questions from Product: how do rollouts and canary deploys interact with tenancy and rollback safety?
[10:24] Luca Patel: Rollouts are at routing layer per model version and can be scoped to routes or tenants. canaries run in parallel on a small percentage of traffic. for Dedicated we can do A/B within same pool or across pools; Private you manage rollout servers.
[10:39] Sam Ortiz: For the pilot scoping, we'll need a test harness for redaction efficacy and a contract clause about handling any observed PII leaks during the pilot.
[10:50] Maya Chen: understood, we'll add that to the pilot scope doc.
[10:56] Aisha Rahman: ok time check — we have about 20 minutes left. can we go over concrete next actions?
[11:01] Maya Chen: Sure. Luca will produce a KMS/residency matrix and an FAQ on logs and retention. I'll share the compliance pack. we'll schedule a dedicated pilot scoping with Tom and Sam.
[11:12] Tom Erickson: sounds good. please include an explicit note about disabling cross-region fallback and disabling KV snapshots for the pilot.
[11:20] Luca Patel: noted. for KV snapshots we'll default to off and use an encrypted-hash option if you want snapshots for performance.
[11:28] Priya Singh: If we want to proceed with Dedicated versus Private, what are the procurement lead times?
[11:33] Maya Chen: Dedicated typically has a few weeks for capacity allocation; Private VPC/on-prem can be 6-8 weeks depending on network approvals. we'll provide timelines in the follow-up.
[11:45] Sam Ortiz: and cost delta roughly? we know it'll be higher for Private but ballpark numbers would help the procurement team.
[11:52] Maya Chen: We'll include high-level pricing bands in the follow-up — not final numbers but orientation.
[12:00] Aisha Rahman: ok final wrap — recap and responsibilities?
[12:05] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to share SOC2/HIPAA pack, KMS and residency matrix, and a pilot scope doc. Hawthorn to share retention rules, sample PII types, and a list of endpoints. Schedule pilot scoping for week of Aug 9th.
[12:20] Tom Erickson: thanks all. look forward to the artifacts.
[12:25] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with the attachments.

Notes on transcript quality: some terms may be mis-transcribed (KV cache as KV cash, VPC as V-P-C) and there was occasional crosstalk.
